football_evidence.question: Can Oklahoma get Mississippi State off the field on third down?
football_evidence.assessment: Most of the 2.3-point difference traces to home field (engine constant) (about 1.1 points), which the closing market has historically priced differently. That explains the gap; it does not make either number a bet.
supporting: When Oklahoma has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Oklahoma’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.2% of its dropbacks, and Mississippi State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Oklahoma has the ball (big plays on the ground): Oklahoma’s offense turns 2.0% of its runs into explosive gains, and Mississippi State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 2.9% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
When Oklahoma has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Oklahoma’s offense averages 3.7 yards per carry, and Mississippi State’s defense allows 4.4 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

Kamario Taylor has completed 102 of 154 passes (66.2%) for 1,450 yards, 9.4 yards per attempt, 17 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in five games for Mississippi State, and has been sacked on 13 of 167 dropbacks.
contradicting: When Mississippi State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Mississippi State’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.1% of its dropbacks, and Oklahoma’s defense sacks the quarterback on 10.7% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Mississippi State has the ball (the red zone): Mississippi State’s offense succeeds on 40.8% of its red-zone plays, and Oklahoma’s defense allows success on 32.3% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
In his last two games (Missouri and Alabama), Taylor averaged 8.6 yards per attempt, against 10.1 in his three games before that.

Parker Puckett has completed 24 of 40 passes (60.0%) for 210 yards, 5.3 yards per attempt, no touchdowns and 1 interception in three games for Mississippi State, and has been sacked on 3 of 43 dropbacks.
